chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Musanna, from Hatim ibn Ismail al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The abandoned child is free; so if he wishes to choose a guardian other than the one who nourished him, he may do so. If the one who nourished him seeks the maintenance expenses from him, and he is affluent, he returns it to him; and if he is insolvent, whatever was spent upon him is considered charity.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for an abandoned child's guardianship and financial maintenance in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of the 'manbuth' (abandoned child) as free, emphasizing their autonomy to choose a guardian other than their raiser. It further delineates financial obligations, stipulating that if the child is wealthy, they must repay the raiser for maintenance, whereas if they are indigent, the expenses are considered charity (sadaqah). This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing the rights of the finder with the child's inherent freedom and capacity.
